The 32 KiB cap matches the explicit portability ceiling and is well below the 49152 maximum, ensuring the shared-buffer estimate 2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*num_stages stays within Metal/GB10-friendly bounds for the feasible candidates. Objective weights are uniform to let traffic, launch count, pipeline depth, and footprint compete without prior bias; footprint uses the same 49152-byte normalization. The FP32 epilogue is assumed to enable buffer aliasing via epilogue barriers, but compiled shared memory will still be validated. Next hypothesis: the solver will favor larger tiles (e.g., 128x128 or 128x64) for traffic reduction, with block_K/num_stages combinations that minimize pipeline stalls while respecting the 32 KiB cap; the first evaluated datapoint will be used to reweight traffic vs. pipeline and to potentially narrow num_stages if estimate/simulator mismatch appears."}
